hypotheses: D1: yes_rate <= 0.05 on floor subjects in BOTH conditions (constant-policy collapse, not partial ability)
D2: accuracy tracks the arithmetic always-no floor, falling from ~0.667 (standard) to ~0.500 (balanced) when items are rebalanced
D3: a discriminating subject shows yes_rate > 0.15 and does not track the floor
notes: Tests whether the 0.6667 always-no baseline is a property of subjects or of item balance. Five of six screened subjects hit it to four decimal places, which is the arithmetic of 8/12 under a constant 'no' policy.
